    tsdst.metrics.glm_regularized_AIC¶

    tsdst.metrics.glm_regularized_AIC(X, Y, reg_mod, unreg_mod, tol=1e-06, method='kawano', family='binomial')[source]¶

    Calculate AIC for a generalized linear model estimated with regularization.

    The binomial and Poisson Kawano correction follows Ninomiya and Kawano’s 2016 paper, AIC for the Lasso in generalized linear models, and the authors’ sAIC R package. The alternative active-coefficient correction follows the Gaussian Lasso degrees-of-freedom argument of Zou, Hastie, and Tibshirani.

    Parameters:
    Xarray-like

    Feature matrix without an intercept column.

    Yarray-like

    Response values. Binomial responses are zero or one; Poisson responses are nonnegative integers; Gaussian responses are real values.

    reg_modfitted estimator

    Regularized model with coef_, intercept_, and the appropriate prediction method. Binomial uses predict_proba; Poisson predictions are count means after the inverse log link.

    unreg_modfitted estimator

    Corresponding unregularized model used for the binomial or Poisson information comparison. The Gaussian branch ignores this argument.

    tolfloat, optional

    Nonnegative cutoff for active coefficients, abs(coefficient) > tol. The same cutoff applies to the intercept. The default is 1e-6.

    method{‘kawano’, ‘hastie’}, optional

    Kawano uses the information-matrix correction. Hastie counts active coefficients. Names are case-insensitive. The default is ‘kawano’.

    family{‘binomial’, ‘poisson’, ‘gaussian’}, optional

    Response family. The default is ‘binomial’.

    Returns:
    aicfloat

    Minus twice the unpenalized log likelihood plus the selected correction.

    Raises:
    ValueError

    If the family, method, tolerance, response, or coefficient layout is invalid.

    numpy.linalg.LinAlgError

    If the active information matrix is singular.

    Notes

    For binomial and Poisson Kawano AIC, let X_A contain active columns of the intercept-augmented design. J=X_A.T @ W_fit @ X_A and I=X_A.T @ W_unreg @ X_A. The correction is 2*trace(solve(J, I)). The ordinary solve follows the named criterion; replacing it with a pseudoinverse would define a different rule. For the active-coefficient alternative, the correction is twice the active count. Gaussian regression uses this active count plus one estimated noise variance parameter, with maximum-likelihood variance RSS/n, for both names.
